_comment: Cross-port pluralization conformance — the already-plural fix. For each `name` (a PascalCase entity short name), `apiPlural` is what every port's API/code-surface pluralizer (TS metadata pluralize / C# CSharpNaming.Pluralize / Java+Kotlin RouteNaming.pluralize / Python apidocs.naming.pluralize) must return, and `legacyPlural` is what every port's FROZEN default-physical-name pluralizer (TS pluralizeTableNameLegacy / C# SourceNaming.Pluralize / Java+Python MetaSource pluralizeInternal/_pluralize) must return. Both are the PascalCase-in-case-insensitive-suffix-rule form; a port applies its own snake_case step before comparing where its naming seam operates on snake_case (Java/Kotlin/Python route pluralize takes an already-lowercased word, so compare case-insensitively or lowercase both sides first).

_collisionComment: Expected-ERROR cases: two DISTINCT entities in the SAME generation run whose API-surface pluralizer output coincides on `collidesOn` — every port's codegen must REFUSE this (a named, cross-port error code, e.g. ERR_COLLECTION_NAME_COLLISION) rather than silently letting one entity's route/hook/DbSet-equivalent name win. Reachable because the already-plural fix makes an ALREADY-PLURAL name's own API-surface plural equal to itself, while its singular counterpart's legacy-suffix plural lands on the exact same string (`Pluralize(singular) == plural == Pluralize(plural)`). Not reachable before this fix — the old suffix-only rule always lengthened the input, so `Pluralize("Address")` ("Addresses") and `Pluralize("Addresses")` ("Addresseses") never coincided.

collisionCases.note: Address (not already-plural, legacy-pluralizes to Addresses) collides with Addresses (already-plural, stays Addresses)
same shape as Address/Addresses — Order legacy-pluralizes to Orders; Orders is already-plural and stays Orders
route-segment twins — the pluralized PascalCase names differ (ApiKeys / APIKeys) but both snake_case to api_key and serve /api_keys

_shapeOnlyComment: Expected-PASS cases: a name collides only inside the scope of the artifact that carries it (one DbSet context, one routes entry, one module or class), and an object that emits nothing (abstract, or declaring and inheriting no source.rdb) takes part in no scope, so it never collides. Every port must ACCEPT each case: build `shapeOnly` and `emitting` as objects in their own packages (`abstract` and `source` say whether the shape-only object is abstract and whether it declares a source.rdb; both objects declare an `id` primary identity, and `emitting` always has a source), then run that port's scoped checks over both. `crossPackageCollisionCases`: two EMITTING entities of the same name in two packages collide when the port puts both in ONE scope (one context, one routes entry); in separate scopes they are two names.

shapeOnlyCases.note: abstract and sourceless: the shape a layered library declares for the application to extend
abstract with a source: an abstract object never has an instance, so nothing is generated for it
concrete and sourceless (#248): no table, route or finder; the adopter owns its data access
the already-plural pair, with one side shape-only

crossPackageCollisionCases.note: two emitting entities with one short name in two packages: refused once both land in one scope, accepted in two
